answer: One workable design: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because shale only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, fable is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any cipher approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
